title: EXPLAINER: What is Red Wednesday?
summary: The Catholic Church in the Philippines is joining the global commemoration of Red Wednesday -- but what is it?

blocks.text: The Catholic Church in the Philippines is joining the global commemoration of Red Wednesday — but what is it?

According to the news website of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines (CBCP), Red Wednesday is a global campaign to raise awareness of religious persecution, particularly for Christians who experience discrimination for their faith.
The campaign began in 2015 when the Catholic foundation Aid to the Church in Need (ACN) lit Brazil’s Christ the Redeemer statue in red to raise awareness for Christians being persecuted in Iraq.

Christian persecution in Iraq has been a longstanding issue. Religious nonprofit organization Global Christian Relief said that in 2014, the self-proclaimed Islamic State rose to power and caused the displacement of Christians in Mosul and other areas.
The CBCP said that the Philippines first joined the campaign in 2017.
By 2020, the CBCP adopted Red Wednesday as an annual Church observance. It is designated as the Wednesday after the Solemnity of Christ the King.

Churches and public buildings across the world will be illuminated in red to remember Christians who were persecuted, according to the CBCP. People are also encouraged to wear red, and asked to pray for the freedom of oppressed Christians.
This year’s Red Wednesday in the Philippines will be hosted by the Archdiocese of Cagayan de Oro. It will be commemorated with a Mass and a candle-lighting ceremony.
The ACN said that there are around 220 million Christians who face religious persecution.
“Let us stand in solidarity with our persecuted brothers and sisters in faith by wearing red and offering our prayers,” the ACN Philippines said, as quoted on the CBCP’s news website. —AOL, GMA News
